unmapped_findings: For the Al-free reference material (Fe-30Mn-1.2C), the best mechanical behavior is the as-homogenized state (360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS, 77% TE); aging leaves YS virtually unchanged and slightly increases hardness, but reduces UTS and TE, with embrittlement most apparent for long aging times (24 h) and higher temperatures (>500 °C). This 550 °C/24 h sample falls in the embrittled long-aging, high-temperature regime.

This sample is the Al-free (0 wt.% Al) reference of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl SIMPLEX TWIP set; no κ-carbide precipitation is reported for the Al-free alloy, so the observed aging-induced UTS/TE reduction is not attributed to κ-carbides in the text.

The paper presents a temperature-sensitive constitutive strain-hardening model for single-phase low-density TWIP (SIMPLEX) steels (three dislocation densities plus twin volume fraction), applicable in principle to this Fe-30Mn-1.2C sample; however, no simulation results are reported specifically for this sample (model validation in Fig. 7 uses a Fe-22wt.%Mn-0.6wt.%C model TWIP steel).
